notes: Making as a trade: seeing and drawing for work, the materials, the state's own craft traditions, showing the work, and the working artist's money and rights. Every check produces a real object, drawing or document. Stance: the traditions named here — the Mardi Gras Indian suit, Chitimacha basketry, the float den, the forge — belong to the communities and families who carry them; this pack teaches the craft with respect and sends the learner to those keepers, never around them.

themes.description: The sketch that gets built: drawing not as art but as the fastest way to show what you mean.
themes.transfer_check: Sketch an object or a plan clearly enough that a second person builds or finds it from the drawing alone.

themes.description: Scale, the ruler, the grid and the eye that checks them: drawing things the size they are.
themes.transfer_check: Draw a room or object to scale with measurements and produce a second drawing at a different scale that matches.

themes.description: One point, two points and the horizon: making a flat page hold a real space.
themes.transfer_check: Draw a street or interior in two-point perspective with correct vanishing points, checked against a photograph.

themes.description: The wheel, mixing, value and the Louisiana palette of water, rust, iron and festival.
themes.transfer_check: Mix and chart twelve target colours from primaries and paint a small study using a limited palette.

themes.description: Where the eye goes and why: balance, contrast, the rule you follow and the one you break.
themes.transfer_check: Produce three compositions of the same subject that lead the eye differently, and explain each.

themes.description: The sign, the poster, the menu board: letters drawn by hand and set by rule.
themes.transfer_check: Hand-letter a legible sign and lay out a poster with a clear hierarchy that a stranger reads at a glance.

themes.description: Gesture, proportion and the human form: the hardest subject and the most useful.
themes.transfer_check: Complete ten timed gesture drawings and one sustained figure study from a live model or a working person.

themes.description: Reading what a client needs, asking what they did not say, and drawing back to check.
themes.transfer_check: Take a brief from a real client, produce three sketched options, and get one approved.

themes.description: The tablet, layers, vector and raster, and the file a printer can use.
themes.transfer_check: Produce a digital drawing with layers and export it correctly for print and for screen.

themes.description: Daily practice: the page a day that makes the hand fast and the eye honest.
themes.transfer_check: Keep a daily sketchbook for three weeks and present the first and last pages side by side.

tracks.name: Materials: clay, wood, metal, textile, paint

themes.description: Pinch, coil and wheel; the kiln, the glaze and the piece that survives the fire.
themes.transfer_check: Make a functional clay vessel by hand or wheel, glaze it, and fire it (or have it fired) to a usable finish.

themes.description: Grain, joints, the saw and the finish: making a thing that stays square.
themes.transfer_check: Build a small joined wooden object — a box or frame — with a proper joint and a finished surface.

themes.description: Cutting, bending, the weld and the forge: shaping what will not be persuaded.
themes.transfer_check: Cut, bend and join metal into a small functional object under supervision, safely, with a clean result.

themes.description: The needle, the machine and the seam that holds: sewing as a working skill.
themes.transfer_check: Sew a wearable or usable textile item with straight seams, a hem and a fastening that lasts.

themes.description: Surface preparation, media and the brush: paint that stays on and looks intended.
themes.transfer_check: Prepare a surface and paint it to a finished standard in two media, with edges a customer would accept.

themes.description: Relief, screen and the edition: making one image many times, all the same.
themes.transfer_check: Cut or expose a block or screen and pull a consistent edition of ten prints.

themes.description: Cutting, setting and grout: the fragile material made permanent.
themes.transfer_check: Cut glass or tile safely and set a small mosaic or leaded panel that holds together.

themes.description: Materials the river and the city bring: seeing the object inside the discard.
themes.transfer_check: Make a finished piece from reclaimed material, documenting the source and the transformation.

themes.description: Sharpening, safety and the shop: a maker is only as good as the edge.
themes.transfer_check: Sharpen an edge tool to working sharpness and demonstrate the safe use and storage of five shop tools.

themes.description: The last ten percent that makes an object sellable: sanding, sealing, polishing, presenting.
themes.transfer_check: Take an unfinished object to a sellable finish and have a maker or buyer judge it ready.

tracks.name: Louisiana traditions: the crafts of the state

themes.description: The Mardi Gras Indian tradition's craft — the patch, the stitch, the year of work — learned with the respect its keepers require.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a small beaded patch with a clean stitch and a finished edge, and describe the tradition's protocols as its keepers state them.

themes.description: Papier-mâché, the den and the parade: the sculptural craft behind Carnival.
themes.transfer_check: Build a papier-mâché or foam prop figure to a design, painted and finished for a parade or display.

themes.description: The balcony, the gate and the scroll: the iron that gives the old cities their face.
themes.transfer_check: Form a scroll or simple bracket in metal, cold or hot under supervision, matching a traditional pattern.

themes.description: Split cane, palmetto and pine needle: the Chitimacha, Houma and Coushatta traditions and the weave that carries them.
themes.transfer_check: Weave a small basket in one traditional technique, naming the tradition and the people it belongs to.

themes.description: The accordion, the fiddle and the triangle: Cajun country still builds its own music.
themes.transfer_check: Make a simple playable instrument — a triangle, a box drum, a cigar-box guitar — that holds tune or tone.

themes.description: The hand-lettered city: the brush, the enamel and the sign that outlives the shop.
themes.transfer_check: Paint a hand-lettered sign in enamel on a board with clean strokes, to a size a shop could hang.

themes.description: Piecing, the pattern and the story in the cloth.
themes.transfer_check: Piece and quilt a small block or panel with a traditional pattern and a straight, even stitch.

themes.description: The pirogue and the Lafitte skiff: the boats the water taught people to build.
themes.transfer_check: Build a scale model of a Louisiana boat from plans, or complete one stage of a full-size build under a builder.

themes.description: The duck in wood: carving, painting and the hunter's eye for what a bird looks like.
themes.transfer_check: Carve and paint a decoy or small figure in wood that reads as its subject from across a room.

themes.description: Newcomb and the state's clay: a tradition of form, glaze and the local ground.
themes.transfer_check: Make a piece in a Louisiana pottery tradition and write one paragraph on the tradition's history from a source.

tracks.name: Showing the work: exhibition and public art

themes.description: The photograph, the file and the portfolio: work no one can see does not exist.
themes.transfer_check: Photograph five pieces to a gallery standard — lit, square, colour-true — and assemble a portfolio.

themes.description: Saying what the work is in plain words a stranger understands.
themes.transfer_check: Write a one-paragraph artist statement, test it on someone outside the arts, and revise it.

themes.description: How a show happens: the approach, consignment, the split, the opening.
themes.transfer_check: Read a real gallery consignment agreement, explain its terms, and prepare a submission to a gallery's call.

themes.theme: The market and the festival booth
themes.description: Selling in person: the display, the price tag, the conversation.
themes.transfer_check: Set up and run a market booth for one session with priced work and a sales record.

themes.description: The call, the proposal, the budget and the community that has to live with it.
themes.transfer_check: Answer a real or mock public-art call with a proposal, a budget and a community-consultation plan.

themes.description: Wall preparation, scale, transfer and the neighbourhood's say.
themes.transfer_check: Scale a design onto a wall (or panel) with a grid or projector and paint a section to finish.

themes.description: Hanging, lighting and the label: the show is made in the last two days.
themes.transfer_check: Hang and light a small exhibition with correct heights, spacing and labels.

themes.description: Giving and taking it: describe, analyse, interpret, and only then judge.
themes.transfer_check: Run a structured critique of three works, and receive one on your own work and act on it.

themes.description: The portfolio site, the post and the shop: being found without losing the work.
themes.transfer_check: Build an online portfolio with priced work and a shop or contact path, checked by a buyer.

themes.description: How work is kept: conservation, the collection and the record of who made what.
themes.transfer_check: Visit a museum or archive and document how one Louisiana work is stored, labelled and attributed.

tracks.name: The working artist: money, rights and the studio

themes.description: Time, materials and the market: a price you can say aloud and stand behind.
themes.transfer_check: Price ten works using a stated formula and compare against three comparable sales.

themes.description: Brief, deposit, contract and delivery: the job that pays before the work is made.
themes.transfer_check: Take a commission from a real client with a written agreement, deposit and delivery, and complete it.

themes.description: What you keep when you sell: reproduction rights, licensing, and the print of the painting.
themes.transfer_check: Draft a sale receipt that reserves reproduction rights and license one image for a specific use.

themes.description: The application: the budget, the statement, the deadline and the no.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a real grant or residency application to submission standard (submission at the artist's choice).

themes.description: Space, rent, the co-op and the shared kiln: where the work gets made.
themes.transfer_check: Cost three studio options — home, shared, rented — and choose one with a year's budget.

themes.description: Sole proprietor, the invoice, the ledger and the receipt you keep.
themes.transfer_check: Keep a three-month artist ledger with income, expenses and invoices, reconciled.

themes.description: The class, the workshop and the school residency: passing it on for a living.
themes.transfer_check: Plan and deliver a one-session workshop in your craft to real learners, with a costed budget.

themes.description: Artist, fabricator, curator, framer, art handler, arts administrator, gallerist, conservator: the jobs around the work.
themes.transfer_check: Map twelve arts-economy roles with what each does and who pays them, and interview one working person in any of them.

themes.description: Councils, cultural districts, the state's programs and the folklife record: the support where you live.
themes.transfer_check: Produce a one-page map of your parish's arts institutions and programs — with what each offers — from sources.

themes.description: The long practice: the year's rhythm of making, showing, selling and resting.
themes.transfer_check: Write a one-year plan for a working art practice with income, making time and two shows, reviewed with a working artist.
